title: Client-side failover and capacity-aware retry contract (idempotency + hedging + kill-switch)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and ship a unified client-side contract and SDK primitives for retries, timeouts, backoff, hedged requests, idempotency keys, and an emergency kill-switch for load-shedding and multi-region failover. This ticket covers the cross-service API headers/metadata, SDK defaults, telemetry events, and a staged rollout plan so customers can opt into stronger hedging or conservative retries while preserving SLOs and cost goals.
scope:
- Define header-level and body-level idempotency key format and TTL.
- Specify hedged request behaviour and when SDK should issue parallel requests to secondary regions or cheaper model variants.
- Establish default retry/backoff parameters per SLO class: latency-sensitive, throughput-sensitive, and background async requests.
- Implement a client-side kill-switch and capacity-aware load-shedding hook that responds to console-driven signals and telemetry.
- Provide SDK change in three languages (Go, Python, JS) and tests, plus runtime contracts for service-side idempotency check semantics.
non_goals:
- Not changing server-side global retry governors (separate infra work).
- Not adding new metrics storage - only reusing existing traces/metrics buckets.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a stable API for IdempotencyKey with auto-rotating namespace and TTL configurable per request
HedgedRequest primitive implemented with configurable hedge_delay_ms, max_hedges, and region_fallback_list
New headers emitted by SDK: X-Redwood-Idempotency, X-Redwood-Hedge, X-Redwood-Client-Timeout and documented semantics
Console can toggle kill-switch per-customer and SDK reacts within 30s when signalled via pubsub/protected endpoint
Automated integration tests cover multi-region hedging, idempotency replay detection, and server-side duplicate-suppression behavior
No increase >10% in median latency for non-hedged requests in canary customers; cost delta measured and documented
decision_log: 2026-02-12 - Team sync: settle on header names prefixed with X-Redwood- to avoid collisions with existing headers. Agreed to keep idempotency keys opaque but length-limited to 128 chars.

2026-02-18 - Infra consult: decided to implement kill-switch as a signed, short-lived token issued by control-plane to SDKs via a customer-specific pubsub topic. SDKs must fall back to local conservative policy if control plane unavailable.
2026-02-25 - Product review: hedging defaults: hedge_delay_ms=75ms for latency-sensitive calls, max_hedges=1, fallback_regions ordered by cost tier and latency profile.

2026-03-03 - Security review: idempotency keys treated as non-sensitive but logged only as hash in server logs; raw keys only appear on client and persisted customer request store where explicitly configured. No PII allowed in keys.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (SDK contract + unit tests) - Add primitives to Go/Python/JS SDKs; unit tests for header emission and TTL semantics (2w)
Phase 2 (Service adapters + integration tests) - Service-side idempotency matcher and duplicate-suppress test harness (2w)
Phase 3 (Kill-switch infra + console toggle) - Publish control-plane topic and SDK listener; safe-fallback behaviour implemented (2w)
Phase 4 (Canary customers + metric collection) - Roll canary to 5% customers, monitor cost and error cohorts, gather feedback (2w)
Phase 5 (Gradual ramp + docs + SDK minor version release) - Cross-language release, migration guide, and deprecation notes for legacy retry-settings (2w)
rollout_plan: Canary: 5% traffic across 3 customers spanning small/medium/enterprise tiers. Monitor p95 latency, error rate, duplicate-response rate, and tokens-per-request.
Stage 1: 25% traffic after 1 week if canary OK. Add a target cost dashboard to track token cost delta vs baseline.
Stage 2: 60% traffic and enable advisory alerts for customers with >15% cost regression.
Global: full rollout following no critical regressions for 4 weeks. Provide opt-out knob in customer console per-route for 90 days post-rollout.
telemetry_and_alerting: New telemetry event: client.retry_attempt with fields: route, hedged (true/false), hedge_delay_ms, idempotency_hash (sha256), region_targeted
New telemetry event: client.kill_switch_activation with fields: reason_code, control_plane_timestamp, sdk_seen_timestamp
Server-side: duplicate_suppressed event incremented when idempotency matcher prevents duplicate action
Alerts: increase in server-side duplicate_suppressed > 0.1% of total requests for a route -> investigate malformed idempotency usage
SLO guards: automatic rollback if canary p99 latency increases by more than 15% or error rate increases by 2x
sdk_contract_examples: HTTP header example: X-Redwood-Idempotency: rdw_1b2f5a... (opaque, client-generated or SDK helper)
JS SDK snippet: client.request({route: '/v1/generate', body, idempotencyKey: client.idemp.generateTTL(300000), hedging: {delayMs:75}})
compatibility_notes: Backwards compatible: if headers absent, services apply existing server-side defaults (no hedging, legacy retry/backoff).
Forward compatibility: SDKs include version header X-Redwood-SDK-Version so server can emit advisory warnings to deprecated clients.
Migration: customers on older SDKs will keep previous retry behavior until they upgrade; provide migration doc and feature flag for early opt-in.
security_considerations: Idempotency keys must not contain PII. SDKs will hash any supplied key before sending idempotency_hash telemetry.
Kill-switch signaling uses signed tokens; SDKs will verify signature and expiry. Control-plane tokens rotated hourly.
Hedged requests follow privacy constraints: no duplicate writes allowed if server indicates non-idempotent action; SDK will disable hedging for routes marked non-idempotent by server metadata.
